built: official birth records only; each place keeps its own publication rules

places.label: the United States
places.rule: Names given to fewer than 5 babies in a year aren't published.

places.label: France
places.rule: Counts are rounded to the nearest 5. Rare names are grouped and not published. Before 2012, France excluding Mayotte.

places.label: Norway
places.rule: Only names used by at least 200 people are listed; fewer than 4 babies in a year aren't published. From 2021, counted by naming year.

places.label: Canada
places.rule: Small counts are suppressed for confidentiality.

places.label: England & Wales
places.dataset: Baby names in England and Wales: 1996 to 2025; Top 100 baby names historical data
places.rule: Names given to 2 or fewer babies are redacted. Spellings are counted separately. 1904–1994: official top 100 every ten years, ranks only.

places.label: Scotland
places.dataset: All names given to babies, 1974 to 2025
places.rule: Every first forename registered.

places.label: Northern Ireland
places.rule: Names given to fewer than 3 babies aren't published.

places.label: Ireland
places.dataset: VSA50 / VSA60: names with 3 or more occurrences
places.rule: Names given to fewer than 3 babies aren't published.

places.label: Austria
places.rule: Before 2010 only babies of Austrian nationality were counted; from 2010, all babies.

places.label: New Zealand
places.rule: Names registered fewer than 10 times in a year aren't published. Years are registration years.

places.label: New South Wales
places.agency: NSW Registry of Births, Deaths & Marriages
places.rule: A ranked list of the most popular names only.

places.label: Queensland
places.agency: Queensland Department of Justice (Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages)
places.rule: Top 100 names only.

places.label: Sweden
places.dataset: TAB619: newborns' 100 most common first names · Namn på nyfödda
places.rule: The name a child is called by (tilltalsnamn). 1998–2022: Statistics Sweden's top 100, with different spellings of a name counted together. From 2023: the Swedish Tax Agency's top list, each spelling counted on its own.

places.label: Poland
places.rule: First names of children registered 2000–2025. 2000–2012: names given fewer than 5 times aren't published; from 2013, fewer than 2.

places.label: Denmark
places.rule: Top 25 names for 1985–1992, top 50 from 1993; spellings of the same name are counted together. Before 1996 only babies with Danish citizenship were counted.

places.label: Switzerland
places.rule: Every first name given in the latest year, with its count in each year back to 2000; a name nobody was given recently may be missing from earlier years.

places.label: Catalonia
places.rule: Top 100 names of babies born in Catalonia each year. Idescat counts accented and unaccented spellings together (Martí and Marti) and shows one of them.

places.label: Berlin
places.rule: One city, not all of Germany (Germany publishes no national list). Babies registered in Berlin. Until 2016 every given name counts; from 2017 only the first name.

places.label: Chile
places.agency: Servicio de Registro Civil e Identificación
places.rule: Every first name registered, even once, 1920–2021.

places.label: South Africa
places.dataset: Recorded live births (P0305), top ten baby forenames
places.rule: Top 10 names only, for births that happened and were registered in the year. 2015–2016 count a forename in any position; from 2017 only the first forename.

places.label: Moldova
places.dataset: Raport statistic privind cel mai frecvent prenume al copiilor nou-născuți (dataset.gov.md)
places.license: Reuse with a link to date.gov.md
places.rule: The most frequent first names of newborns registered by civil-status offices in the year (top 20 in 2018–2022, longer lists in 2016, 2017 and 2023).

places.label: Brazil
places.rule: Names of people counted in the 2010 census, by the decade they were born; 1920 stands for everyone born before 1930.

places.label: Finland
places.agency: Digital and Population Data Services Agency
places.rule: People in the Finnish population register, by the decade they were born, counting every first name a person has (not only the one they go by). Names with fewer than 5 bearers aren't published.
